My Thursday dinner partner ordered a chicken masala or something similar from the menu and had the same complaint as I had from the buffet food - just a large helping of sauce.  All was not lost however.  The mango sweet potato soup was terrific and I really enjoyed their pakora, naan bread and saffron rice, so did not go home hungry.  Can't say the same for friend who ordered from the menu!
By the way, they don't bring your bill to the table so you will be there a long time if you are waiting for it.

This place is amazing! Food, ambience, drinks, service was fantastic! Right from the get go when I called to make resos Bella was very friendly and even asked if we wanted a booth! The day of I called to confirm resos and the girl thanked me for doing so. We got there 10 mins early but our table was ready! Service was prompt, our drinks came out right away and there were tons of menu items to choose from, both for breakfast and lunch! Our food came out in a timely manner too and we all enjoyed what we had. I had the spinach eggs benny (hollandaise sauce was amazing), it came with amazing home made fries/potatoes and fruit. I even loaded the potatoes with sautéed onions, mushrooms, and cheese (it was extra but well worth it)! They even take 10% off the bill if you have AMA! This is a great place for all ages and well worth every cent! So glad there are 3 locations in Edmonton too!

Mmmmmmm....sushilicious!
This would be my favorite Japanese restaurant to eat at in Sherwood Park.
They have a take out side and the restaurant side. I love eating out so you'll find me in the dining room stuffing my face with sushi!
There menu is absolutely great to look at and you know exactly what to order. The sushi, maki and sashimi is created by artistic hands bringing out the arrays of beautiful colors. 
You can also go on there website and look at all the food pictures.
It's a nice looking restaurant, fully staffed, clean atmosphere and friendly service.
Lots of variety of items to choose from and you won't be disappointed, because it all taste delicious. They pride themselves in serving you with the freshest ingredients and it's also prepared by there own chef using traditional Japanese methods.
I've tried a lot of there Maki Sushi and it's absolutely delicious. 
The Emperors Boat was amazing to look at and also very yummy! I haven't tried enough of there food here and must come back for more. I just love the colors and the vast variety of creative edible art. 
It's also kinda cool how they have bubble tea here and it's actually good.  
There's a lot of selections here, so you will always find something new to try.
They have happy hours, a buffet and theme nights. So if you're in the area make sure you stop by at Sumo Sumo.

I'm definitely a sucker for bagel sandwiches, so of course I loved the food here. I got the bacon and egg sandwich on a cheddar herb bagel. Everything was delicious! The only reason it didn't get 5 stars was because of the price. Otherwise it's totally worth trying!

I have been to quite a few Japanese restaurants in Edmonton and area and Sumo Sumo is by far my favourite. You get a variety of options and the food is always fresh and very appealing. The selection of Maki rolls is amazing. Everything I have tried there has been great tasting. One of my fave places to eat.

Went here for supper. Shared apps, rolls and sashimi around the table to allow everyone to have a little of everything. Absolutely delicious. The venu was nice and the service was pleasant and timely. Prices were also reasonable. I will definitely be back.

This was our first time here. Our family of 4 was quite comfortable in the booth seating. I got enchiladas de pollo which I wouldn't get again. They had an aftertaste I didn't like, but I think that's just my own preference as my husband says they were really good. My husband got a Hugo taco and he said he liked mine more but he really enjoyed his as well. My kids got the kids quesadilla (my 5 yo got sirloin on hers, my 3 yo just cheese. I would recommend just cheese. The steak was a bit too grown up for her tastes). We got totopos (housemade chips with homemade salsa and guacamole) and it was AMAZING. We all shared tres leche cake for dessert and it my new favourite in the whole world. 
The atmosphere was fun, good music (at a louder but not annoying volume), a bar and an open kitchen. The decor is really cool as well! This is definitely a smaller place so make sure you make a reservation! 
We will absolutely be back as soon as possible!

My husband and I celebrated our 15th wedding anniversary today. We wanted Chinese food delivered. As long time customers of the Lingnan, we're used to the best. After a bit of review research we decided to try Huku.

The food was delivered on time, hot and amazingly good! Huku gives the Lingnan a run for their money. We will definitely order from Huku again.

This is definitely my favourite breakfast and lunch place. They have the best "homemade" bagels. There coffee is also surprisingly good too. 

It's a quiet place but it's perfect to bring family and friends. Would definitely recommend this place 10/10.

Used to look forward to Sunday Brunch.. but they have implemented many cost saving measures at the price of quality. Miso soup tastes watered down, barely any flavour. Sashimi limits have gone down from 20 pieces per person to 15. There are now limits on certain fish and tempura pieces. Taken away half the menu, no longer able to order fresh rolls from the menu. Price remains the same, gratuity already added for minimal service as it is a buffet. Not to mention the last three times I have gone they have not had toro or octopus available. Disappointed and will probably be changing my all you can eat sushi option.

I went there on Remembrance Day to have breakfast, and the staff treated me like gold, as I was wearing my medals.  After having a terrific breakfast, another customer paid for my meal, which was very touching and also improved my experience there even more!

I come hear regularly and it always great. Staff is friendly and the manager is awesome. I also like coming year because this franchise is originally from Montreal. I remember going to eat there every Sunday afternoon after a long night out. To give you the long and the short. If your in Sherwood park drop by!

This place has gone to cr@p! I don't know what happened, we use to order take out and dine in from here all the time. They have cut back on items in dishes ie. Shrimp, ordered Cantonese chow mein and 1 piece of shrimp in dish. Under cooked food ie. Schuzen beef the batter was raw and undercooked and even the lemon chicken was raw. It seems they have cut quality for dollar value. I hope they can pick it back up, it use to be a great place to eat but sure has slacked off over the last year or so.

Stopped by for lunch. Ordered Crab and Cucumber Salad, Aloha Roll. The food is ok. The decor looks great. BUT the service really killed it. This is my 4th try and i can confidently say that I will never come back!

-----31 Mar, 2014-----
It's a good alternative to Mikado. I am though not a big fan of their buffet...

Walked in to have my shellac polish removed, there was no customers in there and there were three girls in there on their phones and they said they didn't have time to do it because they had one customer coming in in 10 minutes and they were quite rude about it. Luckily there's half a dozen nail places in a 5 minute radius of here.
Their Mango Ice cream is to die for. I just wish that they chose a spot that had more shade and more seating area. Otherwise, no complaints!

UPDATE

I went to Anna again today, and I just had to comment on the fact that the other stylists clients were complimenting my color before my hair was even finished.  I can not EVER say how much I look forward to another awesome color with Anna

This is definitely one of my favorite places for fast food. They usually have a great deal of the day on promoting different burrito. The last time I was there I had the Chipotle Citrus chicken burrito it was so tasty! Those of you who I've never been here it's similar to a Subway in that you get to choose what goes into your burrito. It's all fresh ingredients and easy to get to just off of Sherwood Drive. I always recommend this little place to friends who are in the mood for some delicious Mexican food!

A friend introduced me to this restaurant in Sherwood Park. She is now an even better friend :)

I was very impressed by this hidden gem. It is located off Broadmoor Blvd, in the MillsHaven area of the Park, in the same strip mall as the NAPA auto parts, Curves for Women and a gas station.

The inside is wonderful - booths draped in sumptuous fabrics, a muted atmosphere playing quiet indian music.

We went for the lunch buffet and it was wonderful. Lots of variety - from very spicy to not at all spicy, butter chicken to lamb. Potatoes & cauliflower to luscious soups. A bit of a tip though - when you go to get your naan bread, ask them to make you some fresh ones. If there are ones already out there, they are still great, but nothing beats piping hot fresh naan!

I have since went back with my daughter who has celiac and they were very helpful in pointing out which dishes were gluten free. They even make a gluten free naan bread!!!! She had lots to choose from and was very happy.

Jacqueline, Judi and her team here really know their chocolate.

I was lucky enough to organize a tasting at this location for a group that I belong to and we had a great time. From greeting us at the door to explaining where they get their chocolate from to the full tour to finally, yes, the samples, they were a picture perfect example of hospitality. Friendly, cheerful, engaging and knowledgeable, they really were the whole package.

Because we were in so soon after Valentine's Day (and their chocolate takes 3 days to make!) we didn't get to see the front case full of product, though there was definitely enough for us to purchase. 

From bars to nibs for baking, they've got you covered. We tried a raspberry hibiscus truffle which had me swooning (why would I eat something hibiscus flavoured? It would just not occur to me, though I'm so glad I tried it!) and bars of all different percentages. Everything was a winner.

I have to say though, their burnt white chocolate (which I believe that they call Dulcey) is unlike any chocolate you've ever had. I shared some of it with a friend who said, "This is really something special" after she tried it and that really is the perfect description. It's just magic. If you do nothing else this week, go to Jacek and sample that.

Anyway, these ladies totally deserve your business. The next time you want to purchase a sweet treat for someone special (especially if that someone special is yourself!) make sure you head on out there. You won't be disappointed.

A new fav sushi place for us!
Great quality of food, never a long wait and always friendly service.
The spicy tuna maki and Cali rolls are amazing. Sashimi is done very well !
Totally surprised me.  Great atmosphere, and the sushi is really good.  Loved all of the rolls we tried!

Been here many times. My son just loves the butter chicken ("you can dip the Knan bread it it!" as he puts it) and is always on us to go again. That being said...there is little consistancy. I must admit I have never ordered off the menu...always simply indulging in the buffet. I can honestly say that it's never been bad....but it not always great. Biggest issue I had was them not having a booster available one time (as the couple they do have were in use). Prices are good for families and it offers the kids a chance to try something different without an unreasonable expenditure. When my 4 year old daughter isn't digging the Indian...we simply fill her up on the fresh fruit at the buffet.  I just wish they could get the food to be at it's best consistantly.

Today i had my walk in massage with prenaka who is your dream come true in a massage therapist. I have so many bad areas of tight sore muscles and now thanks to her they feel like butter and i feel lile a new woman! The music was seasonal which i appreciated cause im a Christmasy kinda gal. Also she got into my arms and chest really well since with my job im standing all day with my arms up. (Hairdresser) she knew exactly when i needed to chat to distract and when i needed quiet to relax. She was well worth the expense none of my previous massages compare! I'd recommend coming early for a steam to loosen tough tight muscles it honestly makes way better of a difference. She also said she's bringing in a deal to build your own massage so you just pick what you want worked on for however many minutes.  I can't wait to try that one out and to get some facial reflexology!

Classic outdoor hard scoop ice cream, really good if that's what you want.
Accepts debit and cash.
It was 29°C and hot and dry- but not the ice cream. It was tasty and not too hard, you had to keep eating it at a decent pace if you were going to keep up with it melting.
Best Mexican place in Sherwood Park hands down!  Sampled all of their tacos and they were great. Can't wait to go back.

I love going to great Canadian bagel. I regularly get a cheddar herb bagel with two eggs and cheese. Great quick breakfast and always delicious.  The location is a big weird to find the first time but worth the trek. Only downfall is that they close at 5, so if your stopping home on the way from work you might miss them.

My favourite restaurant in Sherwood Park!  The food is fresh, the restaurant I has ample seating without being overly noisy, great portions, wide variety of choices on the menu and the best sushi in the Edmonton area. You HAVE to try the patio in the summer. ...their misting system keeps you cool and comfortable. 

I have often ordered the large combination sushi/maki platter for events and have never been disappointed. Should you want to dine-in, you'll be warmly greeted, seated quickly and enjoy a fabulous meal.  

Too many favourites to mention. ..  udon, bento box, maki cones, dynamite roll, and try the green tea ice cream. ..  mmmm

I won't be back, there are much better ice cream stops around. I had the mint chocolate chip ice cream in a waffle cone - the ice cream was so overpowering with peppermint extract that it actually left an aftertaste, and the waffle cone tasted like plastic. Considering it cost me $5.75, which is more expensive than everywhere else, I expected much better.

Super delicious breakfast/brunch/lunch food!! Similar to Cora's but with some different choices. I could spend forever looking at the menu because there's so many delicious things to choose from. How do you choose?! 

The staff was great. And they're the kind of place that will sing happy birthday to someone at your table if you drop the hint. It's usually pretty busy, but worth the wait.

This restaurant was a little hard to find, but we persisted as we were really in the mood. Service was excellent, California rolls were fabulous. We also ordered teriyaki chicken bowl and assorted tempura, typically one of our favorite dishes. These also arrived quickly and we quite enjoyed the chicken. The tempura was not what we expected, the batter was more of a beer batter. The shrimp were tasty, but the veggies did not cook up as crisp (likely due to the thickness of them). I think in the future I would stick with tempura shrimp and skip the veggies.  :)
Overall, a great experience, and I would certainly go again.

Admittedly, this was the only place my fiancee and I went to look at suits/tuxedos for our wedding, but our experience with selecting out pieces was one of the most pleasant wedding-related shopping trips we have had.  I made an appointment for an evening in the middle of the week.  I love that they are open until 8 pm, as I have found that most wedding related places are 9-5 on weekdays, and finding appointment slots on weekends can be challenging.  

When we arrived we were greeted and directed to the back section for formal rentals immediately.  I have to say that most of my rave review for Derks is probably related to the sales associate assigned to us for our appointment - I wish I could remember his name.  I knew the colors I wanted the groom and groomsmen to wear, but had no idea about style or patterns on the vest and tie.  Our sales associate did exactly what we needed; he helped us select out patterns and colors and styles that fit into the look we were going for, and made the process easy and fun.  We used up a full hour and a half trying on different pieces and selecting outfits for my dad and our MC as well as the groom and groomsmen.  When my dad went to get measured for his tuxedo, he was in and out in under 10 minutes, despite showing up on his own 20 minutes before our scheduled appointment time.

I particularly like this location because their formal rental warehouse is on-site.  We were assured that if something was off with the measurements, they could pull the correct size from the warehouse at the final fitting.  They also provide day-of emergency service (say if someone splits their pants), and with four rentals, the groom's rental is free.  The rental deposit is $50, with the remainder due when you pick up the suit or tuxedo.  I'll update my review after the wedding, but so far Derks gets two enthusiastic thumbs up.

I knew it would be relaxing, rather like having a nice warm bath.  However, this was a whole different experience!  The tank was large (I'm six feet tall and it was roomy for me) and it really was like being weightless.  It took a few minutes for my body to realize that it could totally relax, but when I did...bliss!  I actually fell asleep at one point.  I floated several hours ago and I'm still totally relaxed, and my back feels fantastic!  I will definitely be floating again.  I highly recommend this for people with joint pain and or back/shoulder issues.

I would like to add to the great reviews for Float Wellness. 

I've been to a float in Calgary before so I was aware of the process. In fact, almost everything was quite similar. 

Upon checking in with the front desk, you watch a slide show with the rules and policies of the Center. The staff will show you to your room which has a pod, stand up shower, bench, hooks, ear plugs, towels, make up remover, bulb syringe (for ears), petroleum jelly (to seal any small scrapes and nicks)and shower amenities. 

After a cleansing shower, you get into the pod (in your birthday suit) and you can float in the darkness or with some coloured lights. There is music for the first 10 minutes and last ten minutes (the signal that your time is up and to get up and shower before they turn on the filtration cycle). 

In the pod is also a pool noodle or a neck pillow to support your head in the water. I used it about half the time and my husband really liked the neck pillow. 

It's easy to fall asleep in the pod. There is no light, the water is body temperature and you're not meant to feel it but I do a little, especially on areas that are not submerged. 

A few ticks: I wasn't able to turn off the lights in my room so it showed through the pod at the opening since the pod does not seal. I would have liked a switch inside the room to turn it off before getting in. 

The ear plugs provided are your regular foam variety. I would have preferred the wax type which is specifically meant for underwater activities. Due to this, my ears didn't get a great seal and they hurt which lessened the relaxation effect for me. I was constantly thinking about my ears. 


Overall, I had a great experience. There are a few areas where improvements could be made but I would certainly come back. And ill remember to bring my own ear plugs next time.
I usually order 'to go' and they are always quick with great service! I live for eggs Benedict and I think tutti frutti does it right!

Very good Chinese food! Family run business. Friendly staff too. 
We go there a lot and very rarely have had a problem, if their ever was a problem thou they don't like to admit mistakes but they will usually fix it right away :) 
Definitely worth trying if you haven't had it before.

We got the Fish Tacos, Chicken Tacos and the Hugo Beef Tacos on a skillet for our main course. We barely ate three tacos between us because we were kind of full from the starter, the hand made tortilla chips with guacamole and fresh salsa. The tortillas were still hot from being cooked and the dips were very good. I didn't have a chance to grab a pic because we attacked it and it was gone quick. The mains were perfection as usual. This was our third date night here and I recommend making reservations because there was only two small tables left when we got there. We seen one family leave because the place was full. Two couples were able to sit that the bar once tables were full. The beef skillet contains peppers and it was fairly hot so if you can't handle the heat watch out. The chicken and fish didn't have much heat just amazing taste. Staff was really good and checked up on us often. I highly recommend.

Went with a friend for dinner on Monday night to check out Sumo Sumo.  Let me start out by saying read other people's reviews and they are definitely right on a few things - their parking lot is pretty weird, the outside of the restaurant has a nice brown patch of dirt to greet you and some of their maki sushi pieces are unusually large.  But those weren't that big of a deal breaker.  The inside is very modern, clean and has a very calm/relaxing atmosphere.

But back to the food.  We split everything (to try more stuff out duh) - started with the seared black pepper salmon tataki ($14) which was very nice.  Came with a ponzu sauce and was cooked perfectly.  Then for sushi, we ordered the dragon roll ($13), volcano roll ($14) and Joe's special roll ($15).  The maki's were all very good but as other people have said, some of the rolls are cut into ENORMOUS portions.  One roll could easily be cut into two pieces.  Not sure why they don't do that as the last two maki orders have 6 pieces each but could easily be 8 or more.  Plus it would be more manageable to eat.  

We also ordered a small maki - spicy tuna tempura maki ($6.75).  Came in 6 pieces and was different than everything else as it was warm.  Decent but I would pass on this one.  For dessert, we split a deep fried tempura green tea/chocolate/vanilla ice cream ($6 or 7).  So total of the bill was around $70+ which is a bit more on the expensive side but we had lots to eat and even had a mini box of leftovers for the next day.

If your in the Sherwood Park hood, it's worth checking out especially if you can go during the "Happy Hour" specials (3-6pm) where they have a bunch of dishes, all for $5.

The owner had contacted me, and apologized for the misunderstanding. He has been very gracious and kind, and hope he continues to run a successful restaurant. I hope I am the last person who loses a reservation.

Sometimes bigger is NOT better...

Sushi is probably the meal I'd request as my last meal before the electric chair, so I'm always on the hunt for new amazing places. I saw the positive reviews of Sumo Sumo and convinced the boyfriend to take a drive to the Park.

The restaurant - though slightly difficult to find - is quite large and nicely decorated. They also have a huge menu, and the prices are very reasonable. The service was good as well.

We tried their salmon and red tuna sashimi. In both cases, the sashimi pieces were just way too big. I don't want to be gnawing on a giant hunk of fish flesh - it's supposed to be melt-in-your-mouth morsels!

We also tried several of their rolls - Samurai Maki, Volcano Maki, Chop Chop and Avocado Maki. The Samurai rolls were easily 3 inches in diameter with smoked salmon on top, making it impossible to eat in one bite and quite possible to end up with pieces of that roll on your lap as you attempted to eat half of it at a time. The Volcano roll was good, but cut inconsistently so there was one pieces that was thicker than an inch, again resulting in mess. If you're a fan of stuffing your cheeks like a chipmunk, you'll love Sumo Sumo's rolls... The smaller maki - Chop Chop and Avocado - were better, but even they were too big. There was so much rice in them, the seaweed was splitting.

There wasn't really anything really wrong with Sumo Sumo. The fish had good flavours and the food was still tasty. If I lived in Sherwood Park I might visit it often, but I wouldn't go out of my way to visit the place again.

I normally go here once a week for lunch. Can't beat 7.00 lunch. Food is fresh. I normally get the black pepper beef on rice. Potion is great. 

Service from Megan is always great. The only thing I would not give huku 5 stars would be at times i go there, they are not open during lunch and is Inconsistent with opening times.

Great sushi & maki in a bright, clean and open atmosphere.

This is my husband's absolutely favorite place to have Maki.  I really like how they have different specials on different nights of the week.  They have PHENOMENAL kebobs there - beef, chicken, veggie - you name it!  I believe it's Wednesday night where all the kebobs are $2.99 each... although it's been a little while since I've been there.

They also have great maki and sushi boats if you want to experience a variety of items with a date or group!

It is a little on the noisy side as the grill is an open concept and when I've taken my toddler there I notice that she tends to be louder than usual to compete with the noise level.

Their desserts are a little overpriced in my opinion - they are frozen sorbets in the shell of the actual fruit (coconut, pineapple, etc.) and they can also be purchased at Costco.

If you're in Sherwood Park - a definite must try!

the bellini tasted lye potty that they scooped up off of their "leather" seats. and survur touched my bf's straw!!!! in wut world do u live in if u think u can touch our straws???????????
n she also touched every single ting on our platter while reciting each fishy's biography and was spittin all over the food. there was literally spit EVERYWHERE. so my bf told her to cum back and give us sum sushi with tha spit. then when she came back she wouldn't stfu and kept telling us that when we come back we'll try bigger and better things. who the fuck gave you the right to tell us what we're gonna do you have brown shit in your nails you don't have the right to talk to us like that!!!!!!!! o and she put the forks on the table not on our napkins thas fucked up if ya'll don't think shes fucked up then ya'll r whack.. n our coasters were small napkins.

I stopped in at Derks today and the experience started off quite negatively. As I was getting out of my vehicle I saw an older man dressed in a nice suit smoking literally right beside the door. Not only do I think this violates a bylaw but it's really disrespectful to any patrons that might be coming to visit the store. Sure enough he ended up behind the counter in minutes.

   Upon getting inside I had to speak with three people before I got any information that I was looking for in regards to a suit. They didn't seem to know a whole lot about a current promotion they had on for a machine custom fitted suit. The selection for the promotion was extremely limited and I ended up not making a purchase.

   Not sure if I would return, but it wasn't the greatest experience.

Ohhhh Sumo Sumo. Come HANGRY (that's so hungry that you're kinda cranky about it and therefore a little angry).

We've stopped by this place on a number of times and it's been so busy that you can't get in for about 20-30 minutes. Thankfully, there's a way around that! As soon as we know we'd like to go, we call ahead to "make a reservation" (even if it's just for the 15 minute drive to Sherwood Park) and haven't been turned down yet.

The selection of specialty rolls is HUGE, and so are some of the rolls we've tried. The Samurai roll was large enough that it needed to be cut into three pieces (a real task with chopsticks, I assure you), but every bite was worth it. The Dragon Roll was definitely the best surprise on the menu, with a spectacular barbequed eel, avocado, and a really tasty eel sauce. We'll be getting that again!

We've also ordered the Emperor's Boat, featuring a sampling of different items, which was a great option to have some rolls that you can get anywhere (rainbow, california), but also try some things we wouldn't normally order, like the spicy crab sushi and spicy tuna tempura maki. It's a perfect size for two people, and definitely cost effective if you're painfully indecisive (like me!).

Don't want to wait for a table? They've also got a great takeout menu, with its own separate storefront for pickup. I may not have sushi directly in the Fort, but Sumo Sumo is worth the quick drive!

I've been to Sumo Sumo at least a half dozen times while in Alberta.  It is probably one of the better places for sushi and sashimi in the Edmonton area.  I think it is worth the drive out to Sherwood Park from downtown Edmonton just for their Chirashi alone.  It is not overly expensive, but in reality, all mediocre to good sushi in Edmonton is going to be pricey.  Face it.  Edmonton is around 1,000 kms away from the Pacific Ocean, so any decent quality sushi in Edmonton will be expensive in comparison to a burger or steak.  The only roll that I didn't particularly care for was the Mexican roll.  Some of their fusion dishes are great, but the the Mexican roll is one that I would pass on.

Tutti frutti is like Trey smith. nobody knows who he is but is still following in the shadow of Coras, who is Jaden smith. both the sons of will smith but one is famous and has a delicious menu and tutti frutti just does not compare although they are both pretty much the same. My food was good. I got ham crepe which I enjoyed but my girlfriend got a Bacon and cheese omelette and the best part according to her was the toast. she didn't finish it and me, being the fiend that I am finished it and it was dry and not a good omelette at all. I don't care though I'll still devour burnt toast just because I like eating. I give this place 3 stars. sorry Trey smith. you will never be the Jaden smith of restaurant. AMA discount was a bonus!  but all in all your still Trey smith...

A little hole in the wall.  Mom & pop shop.  Chinese food was good beer selection mediocre $2.50 for a can of pop.  Dinner for 2 is the right amount of food for 2 people.  A little bit tucked away in business industrial area.  Service is non existent but like I said mom & pop mom reads the newspapers and stares at you

This is one of my favorite places to get Mexican.  You HAVE to try it.  Very authentic, and fresh.  You NEED to make a reservation if you want to dine in (it's just always that busy), but the take out is just as amazing!

Hasn't been the same since they moved...

Decor is nice...and the food is great.

However, the food and decor can't overcome the awful service....and its pricier than other sushi places in the park.

Tried it a few times since the move.....benefit of the doubt as it was new and busy.....but 2nd and 3rd try it was the same way......wont go back due to the service.

We found another sushi place in Sherwood park....less decor and better service and price.

Ordered the chirashi set. Fish. Are a room temperature. I guess I like my fish chilled.

I did appreciate the salad & miso soup the chirashi set came with.

The interior is huge and contemporary- quite different that most little sushi joints I typically frequent.

This review is more for the Take out section. 
Although it is a small room it is worth the wait for a deliciously made sushi. They serve some unique sushi on their menu not like the traditional sushi people normally see, better than Mikado. Plus they have slushies, smoothies, and tea with lychee and/or tapioca my favourite. Menu is moderately pricey but better than the average sushi like Tokyo Express. Parking is large, staff is friendly, atmosphere is semi-cozy in the lobby for take out. No washrooms for the Take out lobby. I have dined in here before and it appears to not have changed too much and is very chilled but can be busy in this area at times, see photos. They do have specials at certain times and days as well.
Recommended for sushi lovers.
If your looking to take someone on a date, this place would be one of my choices.

Looking for a quick, tasty meal that will leave you full (sometimes more than full)?  Burrito Libre is a good choice.

This fast food Mexican restaurant is set up similar to a Subway.  You order from a set number of items on their menu, then customize from there.

To date, I've only sampled their burritos and the sampling has been good.  From pulled pork to chipotle chicken, the ingredients are fresh and tasty.  Decide on the size of the burrito (regular or large - large will leave you with a food baby unless you're a teenager or someone with a hollow appendage), then choose your meat.  My personal favourite is the chipotle chicken.

Now you get to stuff your burrito with a multitude of tasty ingredients.  From rice to beans to peppers to an assortment of salsas, there's something everyone will like.  Don't forget the guacamole, you pay a little extra but it's worth it!

Burrito Libre also offers nice little paper bags of tortilla chips and salsa.  The chips are fresh (must be deep-fried in-store) and tasty, with a hint of lime and salt.

The decor is pleasing, for a fast food joint and the bathrooms are clean.  The staff has always been very pleasant and they work quickly.  If you're in a rush, this is a definite plus.

If you're looking for a quick meal and like Southwestern/Mexican food, check out Burrito Libre.  It's a great change from burgers and subs.

Three adults really appreciated the attentive service of our waiter and all of us enjoyed a delicious buffet.  Although a limited number of entrees we did enjoy the tandoori and butter chicken the best.

The Sunday Brunch menu is quite good... and I rather enjoyed the variety of options available  both on order and from the buffet. This restaurant is pretty great when it comes to the wide variety of options to suit everyone in your group's tastes.

Service was really good when we went and we all got just about what we wanted out of our visit. I was kind of disappointed by the dessert selection and didn't order much from the wait staff, but rather enjoyed the appetizers and other buffet options and the sashimi was pretty tasty (and the pieces were large) so no complaints there! 

I haven't been here recently at any other meal times so I don't really know what to say regarding other meal options.

I'm not a big fan of the traditional music at this restaurant which sets a damper and serious mood. However the service is great which made up
for the sashimi that was frozen..

We used Derk's for my groom, our 3 groomsmen (2 of which are extremely tall), and our 5 year old ring bearer. They all looked smashing and there were no issues with getting proper sizing for our tall guys.

At this location, they have the warehouse on site so grabbing new sizes is super easy. 

When you get a staff member working with you, they're great - you just may have to wait 45 minutes to get one - even when you have an appointment. I'm not sure if there's scheduling conflict issues, or if they just have a crazy amount of walk in traffic (unlikely), but the waiting got a little tiresome. 

All in all, it worked out and I was happy.

Ok
Not great.
Expensive.
Still far better than "McFood".
Personally I find Mucho Burrito a better value.
Fresh enough.
Haven't been in months...drive by often and decide..."I'd rather go somewhere else".
All that being said, it is certainly worth giving a them a shot. It may very well be a good fit for you.

I've been coming to this location almost since it first opened and have continued to go there as often as I can, for a couple reasons.

First and foremost, it's hands-down the best burrito I've ever had, without exaggeration. The salsa has just the right amount of onions and cilantro, the guac (and everything else, for that matter) is always fresh and consistently prepared, the chips that come with the chips and salsa are lightly dusted with lime salt and taste good enough to eat by themselves, the chipotle dressing is to die for, and they're always introducing new types of meats and flavourings to 'spice it up' so to speak. I find myself craving these burritos at least once a week. They also have tacos, quesadillas and burritos in a bowl to add some variety. They even have a kid's menu!

Secondly, the price is quite reasonable. A regular burrito with a drink combo will probably run you about $13, and the food is well worth every penny. Add the friendly and attentive staff (they always thank you as you walk out the door, no matter what), the convenient location just across from the mall and library, the perpetually clean and relaxed atmosphere and the fact that it's open late most nights, and I would never dream of going somewhere else for my burrito fix.

Like Mucho Burrito, Taco Bell or Tacotime? I guarantee you'll fall head over heels for Burrito Libre.

New to the city checked this place
Out and was very impressed by the store it's product and the owners knowledge of parrots . Since they are parrot owners they can understand everything and on the same page . The owners are always happy , know you by your first name and helpful . Even cheaper prices then the mega pet stores . I get 99 percent of my stuff here now as it's just that good . I will be leaving my parrots with them whenever I go on a vacation another bonus this place does ! Nothing but good news here !

I wouldn't say I am a die hard sushi fan by any means but I do enjoy a few things.  I tried the tempura shrimp, the California rolls, and the spicy tuna tempura maki (or something like that).  It was all pretty good.  The menu is huge - a little overwhelming for a rookie sushi eater.  I do find this place to be pretty pricey - although you do get a good amount of food - the portions are more than I can handle by far.

Now let's talk about the parking lot!  There must be some civil engineer in Sherwood Park with a sick sense of humour.  This parking lot is a JOKE - mind you it is still under construction...  There are random meridians everywhere and the puzzle of roads just doesn't make any sense?!?!?!?!  I can only imagine this place must be a nightmare after a huge dump of snow!  Good Ol' Sherwood Park and it's wacky parking lot designs!

I would go back here if I was with someone who was craving it - as a number of people I know do on occasion - as long as someone else was driving!!!!!

Everything was pretty close to on point in this restaurant. The lighting was good not to dark like many Indian restaurants tend to be. The music was traditional not top 40. Decoration were 50/50 some nice ceiling features really hit it home for me and some other wall decor was meh. Now the food, I'm vegetarian so I won't speak on the meat dishes. But great selection for vegetarians. Salad bar needs better labelling so as not to scare people away from trying something new. Couple dishes were oily but that's buffets for you. The biggest down fall in the food was that they did not make naan bread to order made the bread dry and stale. As a restaurateur I see 3 cooks and 5 servers with only 4 tables on a Friday night... make the bread to order with coconut and garlic options. Ice cream machine is great! Banana bread balls in syrup! Amazing! 60$ with a tip for two pops and 2 buffets a little high but I do understand begets have lots of waste to counter act and with low volume on a Friday night. I'm ok with the price.

Found a small black curly hair in my wonton soup 
:( 

I kept eating it because my fortune cookie said to "conquer your fears or your fears will conquer you!"

I won't go back, nothing special.

The best non fast food sit-down Chinese restaurant in Sherwood Park. Their won ton soup is to die for! Their seafood dishes are fresh and delicious. Don't forget to order special tea. It isn't on the menu but they have a huge selection of Chinese tea. Be sure to ask for the Blooming tea! And Megan is the sweetest waitress you will ever meet!

For the most part, a chinese restaurant is a chinese restaurant. They all serve the same food and most of the time you get mediocre portions with excessive soupy mess drowning the veggies and meat.

Huku is good. It reminds me of the Chinese restaurants I visit in Vancouver. Friendly staff, good flavoured food and at a decent price.

Hidden gem in Sherwood Park. Great service and sushi is always fresh. The new location is great for date night or family meal out! 

Sushi boat was excellent and so was the bento meals!
Great for kids!  Lots of options- almost too many!  The service varies by server and day.

I've heard mixed reviews about Sherwood Park's Sumo Sumo, so I wasn't sure what to expect when I ventured out there for my first visit. It's hard to trust people's opinions on sushi because everyone has their favourite dish and not every restaurant will make that dish well. For me, a sushi restaurant that offers light, generously sliced pieces of high quality tuna sashimi will always top the list over another that perhaps specializes in unique rolls. I'm all about that tuna.

And, thankfully, Sumo Sumo does it really well. The menu is HUGE--it took us forever to decide on what to order--and they have a great selection of platters and combinations, for those who like to mix things up a little. We tried the small Maki and Sushi Platter between two of us, which had 8 pieces of California Maki, 2 pieces each of salmon, tuna, shrimp, and egg, 3 pieces of salmon maki, 3 pieces of tekkamaki (tuna), and 6 pieces of kappamaki (cucumber). We also ordered a coupe of a la carte items on the side to satisfy some cravings (more tuna sushi and a sushi pizza).

The service was friendly and efficient and the sushi itself was delicious. The restaurant itself is cozy and perfect for a date night or just dinner with friends and family. The tuna, to my utter delight, was perfect: a nice thick chunk that simply melts in your mouth.

Cost-wise, Sumo Sumo sits about mid-range for a sushi restaurant. Dinner for two with a large bottle of hot sake came to about $70 total with tip, which is fairly standard. I'd definitely eat here again and look forward to getting my hands (or chopsticks) on some more of that excellent tuna.

I've eaten in the restaurant and I've order take out. Was easy to order takeout.

It's quite similar to Coras or any other breakfast place. There are a lot of options on the menu. The options are pretty basic breakfast food. What I've had has tasted good, but not great. 

I'd return if I were looking to have breakfast somewhere in Sherwood Park, but I wouldn't travel or go out of my way to go here.

If I could give this place no stars I would.  I went in based on Instagram photos I saw thinking what amazing work they do. I show the nail tech the picture (all the work done in the pictures was by her) and she tells she doesn't know how to do it.  She told me she didnt know who put the pictures up but its not their work someone made a mistake.  I appreciated their honesty in that regard but their customer service was non existent. When I walked in the owner asked me "what do you want?" I decided not to get my nails done there and walked out.

I live in North Carolina, and I'm here for the summer. I eat at Chipotle Mexican Grill all the time in NC. While Burrito Libre is not as good as the revered Chipotle, it's my favorite fast food in Sherwood Park. Only $8 for a big burrito bowl that I get two meals out of! Plus it's reasonably healthy and pretty tasty. The ladies that work at the front are pretty friendly too. The only thing this place needs to stop doing is piling a ton of lettuce in at the end.
love it! the owners are always friendly and helpful. even if you don't find what you're looking for they can order it for you. best selection of birs toys/accessories ever!!!

Great food, crummy service. The one person behind the counter could not even explain the menu options, let alone provide suggestions.

Study the online menu before you go so you have fewer questions for the incompetent staff.

This place looks impressive but prices are out of this world. Also, this place is not operated by Japanese, but by non-Japanese Orientals.  Therefore, the food is only an imitation of what is truly Japanese food.  Not the same taste or appearance as the real thing.

UPdate: This is a review of the Sunday Brunch:
$35 for up to two hours of Japanese goodies. Delicious!

Reservations are recommended. They serve brunch from 10am-3pm and this place is packed.

Service is a mandatory 15% , and it explains why this Sunday All you can Eat buffet is worth it.

The problem with most all you can eat sushi places in Edmonton isn't their lack of food quality , it's their lack of SERVICE quality.

It's like they have this idea that "sure it's all you can eat....but good luck finding somebody to take your next order.....like a ninja we shall hide....until you are sick of looking for us and leave....heh heh he"

Sumo Sumo has a quick turnaround for repeat orders (7 minutes from order to food coming out) and always easy to find a waiter.

Sumo Sumo has a traditional buffet area, and waiter service, so if you do get hungry waiting for your order you can go graze at the buffet. Which, does have assorted maki rolls, gyoza, yakitori etc.

No discussion of an AYCE place is complete without loopholes , limitations and errors.

1. 20 pieces of Sashimi per person , (loophole: They don't care if it's more than 20 per PERSON as long as the table doesn't get more than designated. I always bring my Sashimi hating gf, so I get hers too)

2. 3 pieces each of the really good sashimi. (Loophole: You can still order the expensive sushi that has the same pieces on it)

3. 2 hr timelimit. This honestly has never come into play. We always are out under an hour.


5 stars!

Pros:
Great value
Free Parking
Good Sushi/Sashimi

Cons
HORRIBLE Desserts (seriously). Ok not horrible, but it's those crappy square bar things you always find at horrible dessert places. 
Hot dishes could be more "hot" they don't fill pans enough. They should make more small portions, by the time the Gyozas are empty the last few are less dumpling and more soccer ball.

We had dinner at Sumo Sumo for the first time on Friday, and it was delicious.
The staff were friendly, the food was fresh and the decor was very nice!! We will most definitely recommend this restaurant to all of our friends. Even our non-sushi friends found menu items to enjoy.

I like this location because it usually isn't too busy and you can get in and out of the store quickly. However this area is building up quick with other stores and soon will be just as busy as other Walmarts.

Lots of large portions. We got the seafood dinner bento which was on special for Tuesday. 19$ from 27$. It was definitely a good value as there was tons of food. Most of the food was decent; however, there some weird things such as the teriyaki sauce on the beef which tasted very edo-ish. But sushi was satisfying and the volume  of food really spoke to my stomach!

They also went all out on the internally and externally. This is evident from the time you cross the bridge to the large temple-esque entrance. Internally screams modern Asian-esque design!

Service was very quick and good. Very to the point. They answered all question we had quickly. This is service with the goal of getting the job done! 

3.5 stars round up for a fun atmosphere.

Picked up naan, rice, and vegetarian samosas for 4 ppl to compliment a couple curries I made myself.  $65 later, the naan was an elastic mess with no flavour or seasoning, the rice was already hard and dehydrated, and the samosas were so unlike any delicious handmade samosa I've ever had.  Seasoned incorrectly, completely homogenous in texture, and lacking any of the character of freshly roasted spices that samosas made with care usually have.  It was garbage, robotic food.  I wouldn't have a problem with sides like this being as horrifically expensive as they are if they delivered quality - but these were sub par for even half the price.  Too bad - New Asian Village made a name for itself based on quality - sad to see the satellites coasting on coat tails.  This food was crap.  Will never go back.

Sumo sumo..get the spciy tempura maki..I never liked eating sushi at all then I dated this chick and well its all we ate. I was the one who always paid so price is good, descent.  Its all the way in the park which is ok? I hear they are opening a new location which is good cause parking righ now is ill. Service is fast and friendly. So if your the paying one ion the realationship sumo sumo is a good place to getlarge portions for a wicked price.
St.Patricks day to enjoy Caladh Nua,Irish traditnl folk music at FP,with my bride.Enjoyable.

Sumo sumo makes half decent sushi, but if you can get out if there for under $40 per person then you are probably going to walk out hungry.
I have been to sumo sumo a number of times because I forget how expensive it is or my wife forces me to go, but I've had enough of $100+ bills for lunch for 4 people AND leaving hungry.
How can 1 roll cost more than $10? Well they don't have any under $10, in fact they have a 6 piece roll that costs $15 for one roll! I could buy a premium side of salmon for that.
Amazingly fresh food and incredibly hospitable staff. We will definitely be back!  Loved it!!!

I've visited their food truck many times and have loved their food. The restaurant was not as good though. The margaritas were made with bottled lime juice, which was a disappointment. It took a long time for anyone to serve us, as well as to get our drinks and the appetizer we ordered. It took so long that we hadn't finished by the time our main course came and they took our appie away when we hadn't finished it! The tacos were very good though as usual. Not sure I will drive out to Sherwood Park to the restaurant again, but will for the food truck.

Wow! Great Mexican food in Canada! I am from the States and found myself North of the Border on business. Looked into the reviews, being skeptical decided to give it a try with our group. I have to say it was very good. The menu selections were not overwhelming, but what they had was done extremely well. I had the enchiladas and asked for them to be spicy expecting it to be mild, but it had a great spicy flavor. The Margaritas also seemed to be homemade instead of the usual mix variety. Chef came around and welcomed each table. Would highly recommend.

Good selection of sushi, rolls and other food. The bento box supper is HUGE but really good! The patio is one of the best in town. Usually not too loud and very accommodating towards kids.
The joes special roll is delicious.

Been eating here for 7 or 8 years. Still the best burrito in the city. Wish they would expand faster. I'd like to make it a food truck. Guacamole is fresh not packaged like other leading brand burrito joints. The corn is great! The portion is beyond an excellent deal. They have great tofu option. And amazing chocolate cookings make with caramel. If you like burritos and haven't tried your missing out! It's even better than chipotle! Go go go Arrrriba!

Wow. Just Wow. I had been to the old Sumo Sumo when it was just a small diner like cafe that would only seat about 20 people. I had NO IDEA they had made such a dramatic change with this new location.

First of all, the decor. Gone are the cheap chairs & table with little to no sense of privacy (sitting in the lap of the diner next to you wasn't much fun) replaced by  white leather modern/oriental decor. Lots of black - including black granite table tops - made the white leather pop. The water treatments helped create an even more soothing feeling and ambience.

The food was wonderful. We are not big sushi eaters (sorry!) so we had the bento boxes. The gyoza was a wee bit oily, but that tends to be the nature of that dish no matter where you get it. The tempura was crisp and flavourful.

I had the chicken and ribs combo and my husband had the chicken teriyaki. Both were very good, hot and full of flavour. The rice was tender without being mushy.

I really liked the fact they didn't just bring all the food out, plonk it in front of you and leave. I have had that experience many times at Japanese restaurants in particular. Here, they brought out the sides first, waited until we were finished before bringing out the main entree.

The service was incredible. At one point I mentioned to my husband that when the waitress came around next, I would need a new drink. I had barely gotten the words out of my mouth when the waitress appeared and set a fresh drink in front of me. It was like she read my mind!

Our dinner for two -  including green tea ice cream - came to about $50.
Just try the burger. It shames the actual burger places. It's a decent place and offers good value for your buck.

I love this place!

Went to this location for the first time with my boyfriend a few months back and had the titanic. Needless to say it was amazing! Even the presentation was spot on!! 

I came back today with my bestfriend and we had the dynamite roll and California rolls.. Again amazing! 

The only reason why I'm giving a 4 star review is because the first visit our server was a little rude and would chat for 5 minutes at a time with her co workers at the front desk and you could hear the tables around us complaining about tardy service.

A nice venue. Have performed on the stage and had no problem and watched my daughter perform on it. Most of the seats are good aside from the ones on the side which I don't care for. 

It is very crowded in the back during competitions as it is a little small. I live in Sherwood Park so it is my favorite venue for competitions (5 mins away)

AMAZING!!!

The food is awesome and the staff are incredible!!

We went to have lunch and had ordered an appetizer we hadn't realized was breaded. One of our party could eat it due to an allergy.  To my surprise they not only cooked another version but did that without any asking or prompting. The food was wow!

Suggestion: try the calamari cooked without coating - they cooked it in a pan and melted in our mouths!

The place to be on a Saturday morning! Fun breakfast menu. Friendly service but a little slow because it was so busy. Unfortunately meant we didn't get to sit back and enjoy as we were on a timetable. Fruit options were good. Cappuccino was just average. Overall though would go back as a good family option.

I'd been wanting to experience "floating" for a while so I decided to take the plunge (no pun intended). I have anxiety and ADHD and thought it would be very difficult to get to a state of relaxation. I searched around for good reviews and an affordable price and Float Wellness was the front comer. 

Making a reservation here was super easy, with online reservations and payment it made for easy check-in. It allowed you to book in advance and even bank floats for a later date. Which really comes in handy when you've found a great deal or float package. 

Upon arrival we were greeted by the studio owner Lara. Her calm demeanour and warm welcome made my slight anxiety of this new experience drift away. She gave us with a quick power point presentation on an iPad about the dos and don'ts and guided us to the float pod for review. I never felt rushed, you're on float time here! After a go over of the house rules I was left to get ready for my float! 

Float Wellness only offers 90 min floats, which I couldn't imagine floating for any less. Upon entering the tank you're guided with soft music which slowly goes to silence in about 10 mins. You have the option to have soft lighting, or complete darkness. I recommend complete darkness once you're comfortable. It took me about 20-30 mins to get to the state of relaxation. My first experience was a little bit of everything! Being isolated with only your thoughts isn't as calming as one would think, but once you get the hang of it you really do benefit! I'm not sure if I fell asleep or not, but I was in a very relaxed state. About 5 mins before your float comes to an end you're gently woken by the same soft music, a nice way to be guided back to reality. 

Noteworthy... 

-Float in the nude, less distractions! 
-Do not touch your face, the water will burn your eyes! Take advantage of the spray bottle if you do get the float water in your eyes.
-Try different body positions, my choice was hands behind my head. 
-Use the earplugs! 
-Keep the tank door closed, it keeps the heat in
-Don't nap before, and no caffeine before either; it's too stimulating. 
-You will notice every ache your body may have, this is normal. 
-Lay back and enjoy!

STAY AWAY from this place. I walked in yesterday asking to confirm a pedicure fee. The place was empty. When she told me the price I asked why they were higher than the Q-Nails northwest location. She said because they are a franchise so they can. I told her the whole point of a franchise is consistency which included pricing. I said it was akin to going to McDonalds and finding different prices - she and the other girls (who were sitting doing nothing) all began to laugh and the girl told me that it wasn't the same at all...I naturally walked out and went to Binhs in Emerald Hills - they were packed but I waited and got great service with a smile. Girls were polite and prices were much better than Q-Nails Sherwood Park location only. When I shared my story with others waiting at Binhs they had heard stories of the rude women at Q-Nails as well. I would NOT recommend this Q-Nails location due to the rude woman and her associates - they are obviously new to owning a business, knowing what "franchise" means and most importantly knowing nothing about customer service.

At first glance, I saw Sumo Sumo as a Japanese restaurant with all the Japanese culture ripped straight out of it. Fortunately, I'm not judging this restaurant on its culture. I like the space its in and there is a good element of style and privacy going on with the layout and decorations in the place.

The menu seemed approachable enough despite not having a whole lot of lunch options. The Sumo Combo Bento at $15 makes for a pretty good meal - some salad, miso soup, California rolls, a salmon nigiri, and a beef/chicken/shrimp stir fry to get the blood flowing. It's definitely better than that Edo on most days. 

There are three things that I couldn't quite figure out about Sumo Sumo though: The men's/women's signs on the door are the same shaped person but in red or blue so it'll take some soul-searching to figure out where to go, the bar tucked at the back seems busy enough but I can't imagine why anyone would want to hide there, and lastly, the wasabi is not real wasabi but rather a green vaguely spicy thing.

The value is at lunch is right and the service is nice but not terribly quick. I can definitely see why people pack the place at lunch but there's definitely better places for seafood in the Greater Edmonton Area.

Went here again for the second time with a group of 7 for a friend's birthday on a Saturday evening.  We ordered a ton of food but I wasn't impressed this time around.  This is what we ordered:

Appetizers
- 4x Raw oysters in ponzu ($13 for 6 pieces) - so we had 24 oysters. Some were pretty good but others left a really grimy taste in my mouth.
* 2x Salmon sashimi ($14 for 8 pieces ) - beautiful presentation. Part of the salmon sashimi was made into the shape of a rose put on a block of ice.  This was probably the best dish we had from our dinner!
- Shrimp tempura ($13) - nice sauce, but pretty ordinary.
- Vegetable tempura ($10)
- Beef tataki ($14) - I didn't try it but my friends that did said they liked the onions more than the beef. Not a good sign when the beef should be the star of the dish.

Rolls
Good
* 2x Passion roll ($10) - these were good. Slick presentation and had a nice saucy kick to it with the mayo. 
- 2x Joe's Special roll ($15) - this is one of their most popular rolls.
* Dragon roll ($13) - yummy with eel, avocado, green onion over a tasty eel sauce
- Apprentice roll ($13) - different with a light mango mayo sauce
* Spicy scallop maki ($4.50) - you get 6 small makis but these are good. Nice spicyness to it with sesame seeds on top.

Bad
- Spider maki ($13) - normally I love spider maki but the rice in this one was not done properly. The roll was chewy.
- Mexican ($12) - this one was bizarre. They put tortilla chips, salsa and avocado surrounding the rolls. The rolls were unmemorable.
- Sumo roll ($12 for 8 pieces) - these are absolutely massive rolls. Still don't understand why they make them so big. Real sushi your supposed to eat in one bite - this one takes two.  Same problem as the spider maki - texture all wrong.

Dessert
* Tempura fried ice cream ($8.50) - had this once again. It was good but not as good as the first time I had it. The tempura wasn't very crispy. But the different ice creams in it were good - chocolate, green tea and coconut.
* Mango and tapioca pearls on mango shaved ice ($6.00) - refreshing and light dessert. Perfect way to end our meal. 

Note - The * indicates the dishes I liked/would order again 
 
Overall, service very friendly. We were put in a separate booth area as we were a large group but the food is not worth the price. Our bill was something around $280 before tip. Plus, the massive sumo rolls just aren't appealing to me. Not worth driving all the way out to Sherwood Park (lucky me I was in the east area beforehand).

This is by far the best place in or around the park. I've been going to see Molly for a few years now and she never disappoints! Staff are always incredibly friendly and my appointment is constantly full of laughter. If you haven't been here yet I suggest giving it a shot. You will not be let down by these gals ;)

I adore that Jacek has a stand at the OSFM Farmers Market, it gives me an excuse to buy their chocolates (they also have them at Credo sometimes). 

These chocolates are to die for, they are so good. However, they also come with a heafty price tag. I think it's close to $3 per chocolate, but I say well worth it! 

Jacek has very different combinations of fillings inside their chocolate (pb and jam, rootbeer etc.) they are really quite intriguing. They also have seasonal items and the spring line loks divine! You can also order some of the chocolate online incase you don't want to drive to Sherwood Park and can't make it to the market on Saturdays! 

I'm not sure about you but when I hear handmade couture chocolate, I say count me in! These chocolates are really fantastic and would make excellent gifts! I really want to try the sipping chocolate because really who can say no to sipping chocolate...that just sounds silly.

Great event and love attending but really who buys your wine? They have managed to find the most undrinkable cheapest garbage and passing it off at $35.00 a bottle! Come on it is very easy to find reasonably priced wine with great reviews. We bought a bottle and had to leave it untouched. Used to love attending but feel a bit taken advantage of in this department.

This Tim Horton's had a bit of a rocky start in my opinion. When it first opened up a few months ago, the service was EXTREMELY slow. I would avoid going because my patience just didn't last as long as the lineup.

My favourite Tim Hortons, just down the road closed for renovations and I was forced to go to this one. Luckily, the staff at the renovated store were transferred to this new one and the service skyrocketed.

I am hopeful that the more senior (and much faster) staff that have spent the last month at this new Tim Hortons have now trained the staff in their ninja-fast ways.

For now, it is a quick and efficient stop for coffee, but I am going to take a wait and see approach when some of their staff returns to the old Timmies to see if things have improved.

I dropped in here for a quick bite while I was in between appointments. I was alone and was looking for somewhere quick and simple. This fit the bill exactly. The menu has a bit of a Denny's feel to it and I ordered a burger. I was shocked when she asked if I wanted soup or salad with my burger. Then she wanted to know if I wanted fries or hash browns?

I was a bit taken aback by all the options for a simple burger and my jaw dropped when my food arrived. There was enough food for two people! 

A large salad, hash browns, cheese and bacon burger and a bowl of soup. Way more than I had anticipated but I suppose it is better to feel you received your moneys worth than feel you didn't!

The burger was decent, but not spectacular. The salad was nice and fresh and not your typical iceberg lettuce style that I would have anticipated at this type of establishment.

The hash browns were made from real, unfrozen potatoes - a really nice touch.

Overall, it was decent food and a Denny/Albert's type ambience.

Such a lovely place for food.  The people that work here are so friendly and the service was great.  Great food. Cheap prices,  good sized portions, cheap drinks too.  

Give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

Nice little restaurant, gets busy. Food is good, reasonably fast. The one huge complaint is that if there is room they always try to jam you into the seats next to the bathroom, NO ONE WANTS TO EAT NEXT TO THE BATHROOM! If there is no room fine, but if It a beautiful morning and there is room at the same size table at a window place your customers there!

This is a good place to go for your standard run of the mill breakfast (eggs, greasy bacon/sausage, pancakes, hashbrowns, toast, etc...). In my opinion the food is comparable to your Albert's, Smitty's, Denny's (Denny's - EW!) quality of food, but the prices are seriously dirt cheap!! Like cheap to the point where you start to get the too good to be real feeling and begin wondering what it is your missing that isn't right about this place?!?! I don't know but I haven't found anything yet really. 

Been here a few times now and haven't ever really been disappointed. Nothing overly special about the food, or the service, or the decor. However, for the same thing you would order at Albert's (bacon and eggs for example) for $10 bucks, you will get at Clark's for $5 bucks.... 

Although the seriously low prices make me somewhat weary for some reason, I have never been sick after eating there and the food tastes as good as it would anywhere else I think. That's saying something I guess. I'll be back there again sometime I am sure! ...Oh, and they have food other than breakfast - I just haven't tried it ever.

Been to this place probably 3 or 4 times now. The food is really good. The service staff could be better. Twice now I've had an impolite waitress. What really bothers me the most is the amount of black flies in this restaurant.  Every single time I've went to tutti Fruitti theirs always a lot of them buzzing around and bothering people, landing on our food, etc....it's unsanitary to have that amount of flies in a restaurant. If this problem improves so will my review.

I had a wonderful experience at Blaze pizza's newest location in Sherwood park. I got a build your own pizza which was fun to create and it only takes 180 seconds in their fire oven to cook! My favourite part was the wide variety of toppings to work with. Great service, friendly staff, I will definitely be back again. Looking forward to trying out more pizza combos!

If you're looking for fresh sushi this is definitely the place to get it! Very nice restaurant with a lovely patio. A lot of variety for seafood or non seafood sushi lovers, also a nice place to celebrate with friends or have a great date night!

Seriously love this place!!!! I have followed around the food truck for years and when I heard they were opening a brick and mortar I knew it was a place I needed to support. You won't be disappointed. I have dined in Mexico many many times and I can say 100% this food is as close to authentic Mexican dining as you are going to get here in Canada. Don't walk RUN to this place now and get one of EVERYTHING (because you can't choose just one).

This is my favourite restaurant in the Edmonton area!

Everything is awesome. Very clean. Nice and comfortable. Service is perfect, on top of all your needs but not hanging around the table. They always ask how if the foods ok which is a good sign. Bad restaurants don't even ask cause they know. Little pricy but it's sushi in Alberta what do you expect.
Iv been here over 20 times and every time it's been perfect. To eat in or take out if you like Japanese/sushi type food this is for you. I have not found a sushi place better. Way better than Makados and that's saying something!

Overall great experience every time we go to Sumo Sumo. They always show great creativity and an unique approach to their dishes. Sometimes the price can be a bit steep but you need to remember you are paying for an over all experience. Great atmosphere and and food. I have always found them to be very generous with their sashimi. Always thick and of great quality.

This was an amazing sushi restaurant! I have tried over a dozen sushi joint since I moved to the Edmonton area and always left disapointed. Not when I went to Sumo Sumo, the food was outstanding, the service was great, and most of all they also have bubble tea! My love affair with Asian cuisine will continue. The price wasn't too bad either!

Tonight was my second visit to New Asian Village in as many nights while in town on business. Ordered Goat Vindaloo from the menu the first night. Paired with the fresh naan it was superb. Couldn't wait to get back. Ate from the buffet tonight and was impressed by the numerous fresh choices. Service was warm and personal provided by the owner Monika. Looking forward to my next visit. This new find is going to be hard on the goats.
This is a total hole in the wall place. Bagels are made fresh every morning. Not rock hard like Tim Hortons.. Great Service... very personal.

Stopped in at Sumo Sumo for impromptu dinner on a Friday night.
No reservation had us relegated to the "patio"...
Well...patio has a roof, windows and heaters. Impressed allready. Haven't even been seated yet.
Impressive menu. 
Settled on seafood bento box. Substituted yakiskoba for rice. Cost an extra dollar. 
Delicious!
Crab and cucumber salad.
Chicken spring rolls.
Gyoza.
Salad, soup and ice cream also included.
$60 bill for myself and wife with one beer and an iced tea.
Only minor complaint is that each component of the bento "box" was served seperately, and it was slightly confusing.

Great value.
So full!

We will most deffinitely be back!
The restaurant with a modern decor. The food are well presented and taste really yummy. Service was good. However, it's quite pricey. Overall it was a good experience.

Just got off the plane and was starving . When I travel I want to eat somewhere different . I stumbled on this place and decide to go in. Place was clean and food was well prepared and seemed to be freshly made to order as advertised . I enjoyed spicy chicken sandwich with pickle on top but the size of it was a little underserved for the price . The service was hard to understand because of cultural differences and this needs to be improved . Drink selection was mainly bottled drinks which consisted of sugary drinks . Maybe having fresh tea or water could be an option ,

It was a late night and I was hungry but at the same time trying to avoid greasy fast food joints which brought me here to this place. Wow was it ever good! I don't often make the mmm mmm good noise when eating but one bite of my honey sriracha chicken burrito and I didn't care who was around to hear me.

It was positively stuffed with some of the freshest ingredients I have ever tasted. The salsa they have here is delicious and not so hot that it overwhelms the other flavors. I think I paid $8.79 for the burrito and a bottled beverage and I can't remember any other time that I was able to get something that good for under the $10.00 mark.

The staff here made an already great experience even better with how polite and efficient they were. I was in here at 9:15 and despite the fact they were closing in 45 minutes they encouraged me to stay and eat my food even though I offered to take it to go to get out of their hair so they could do their closing procedures and not have to worry about cleaning up after me.

I can't say enough good things about this place but I will just stop rambling here so you can check it out for yourselves...trust me you will be so glad you did!

I stop here from time to time for the odd thing like a household cleaner or something for lunch but I could never fathom doing a whole grocery trip here. It is nothing against the staff as I think they are all lovely. It really has more to do with the prices and selection. Compared to other stores like No Frills or Save on the prices seem pretty steep. I also find the freezer section as a whole to be chronically understocked as well as parts of the deli area. With that being said though they do have a beautiful floral section and are one of the few stores I have seen that keep it well staffed. Alot of the other ones I find if you need help you are running to customer service to get them to page someone. I get why others like it it just underwhelms me in too many areas to make it a regular weekly stop.

I've long been a fan of the Casa12doce food truck so I was super excited to try the restaurant. The food is everything fans of the food truck love, with way more options. And the service is super friendly and awesome. I just wish I would have made a reservation ahead of time but the wait time
Wasn't bad for a Saturday. Will return.

A beautiful venue, very clean and modern. Parking is ridiculous, as the parking lot is around the corner from the main entrance, and staff always takes the closest spots to the door. One woman in the ticket office is EXTREMELY rude and very unhelpful. I would watch out for her if you go in to buy tickets on a Saturday morning.
Taste is good, but fried salmon bowl serving is not enough for lunch, even not enough for girls.

This place left me unimpressed. We came to look for a black suit rental for our small wedding. The rentals are very low quality and cheap looking and are definitely not stylish. The staff are unhelpful and rude to each other and their customers. We decided to go elsewhere.

Stopped in to check this place out and ordered take out for dinner. Restaurant is very nice and modern. Staff was definitely still learning but they were friendly and offered us free tea while we waited for our food to come out. Food was absolutely delicious, good portions, meat was super tender and all was perfectly cooked. Happy to have such a great restaurant close to home. Check this place out for sure, it's in a new complex off of broadmoor so it's kind of hard to spot right now because there are still a lot of buildings under construction.

- this place is not authentic, very westernized
- the Sushi is very complex and tasty with a number of different sauces including barbecue sauce depending on what you order
- patio is great on a sunny day
- good selection of beer, suki, etc
- service was good and fast 
- decor is very modern

Went to tutti-frutti on Wednesday morning for breakfast was really disappointed to see such a booming restaurant so quiet. It's understandable why , the service was so poor , the server seemed to really dislike her job although she was attentive she took care of us while our original server did not. Server 2 took our order , server 1 didn't even come back to check on us . This may explain why the restaurant isn't busy. Food was mediocre.

Reservations are pretty much needed to guarantee a seat. Worth  the effort. Food is fresh, super tasty and served hot out of the kitchen. Margaritas are top notch. It's just good quality, authentic food; hearty portions to fill the hungriest diner.

they always make the perfect burrito. they staff are always so polite and quick, the place is always looking clean and inviting. I highly recommend grabbing a bite from here! and I can't say no to a Peach Stone drink.

Yum Yum Yummy!  I was a regular at their West End Location and miss them to bits!

This past weekend was the first time I had visited their Sherwood Park location since the West Edmonton location closed.

This one does not have a drive thru and the parking lot can only be entered from one driveway; if you miss it, you have to drive all the way around the block :-(  As I did!

Anyhoo, when you do finally make your way in you will not be disappointed in the quality of their fabulous bagels and bagel sandwiches!  I tried the pulled pork for the first time on a jalapeno cheddar bagel and it was killer!  I def miss frequenting them for a sausage, egg, and cheese breakie jalapeno cheddar bagel.

They have coupons in the SUTP book and are a student discount card supporter if I'm not mistaken.

Friendly staff and great quality bagels - hard to get much better than this!

So why only 4 star?  I miss the Edmonton location and drive thru convenience.  For those of you that live or work in Sherwood Park, you are lucky ducks and I envy you!
Great quick place to go for lunch. Prices are decent but the spicy pizza sauce is what will have me coming back. Great addition to the Emerald Hills Area
AMAZING FOOD!!!!! Super pricey. Gotta spend like $50 between 2 people just to get a couple good things. But SOOO good.

Imagine the Jubilee Auditorium - but smaller. The theatre in Festival Place is about half the size, which means every seat is a good seat. The first few rows are actually tables set up cabaret style. Many excellent folk and roots acts come here instead of Edmonton venues because of the intimacy. Ticket prices are a lot lower also. The spacious lobby areas has a bar and there is also a banquet room for meetings and weddings. While getting out to Sherwood Park is not convenient for everyone, the concerts here are excellent.

We used Derk's for my wedding party because I got a gift voucher for them. One was for a FREE groom rental and up to 3 groomsmen tux rental up to $1000.

I called the day before and booked an appointment. When I got there the host insisted we had no appointment, but she would get us the next available consultant. We waited about 30 mins for someone to help us out.

Then the lady who helped us was nice and then she started to get ruder and ruder. We picked the grooms tux, vest, and bow tie and it was good. Then she said OK so all the groomsmen will just match his bow tie, their vest and the tie. But she never asked if we wanted to get another color or style, so as of now I don't even know how the groomsmen tuxes look like.

Also Derk's does not understand their own gift voucher. The lady just multiplied the tux rental price by 4, and charged us the total amount. It clearly stated that the grooms tux is FREE so we should have never of been charged for that. So we ended up having to pay the difference after the $1000 was deducted. I asked her to book appointments next Saturday so all the groomsmen to come in and she just ignored me and booked the final fitting appointment and said have a good day, and preceded to help someone else.
